front.zh: 現代俳句 & 變奏   系列《38》

en: Along the thin mist of evening
Wandering in for no reason, that year
The single note you left behind
Turning to look back at the road I came by
Distant mountains without rain, the trees without wind
One by one, dusk begins to color them

points.zh:
「 三月七日，沙湖 道中遇雨。雨具先去，同行皆狼狽，
余獨不覺，已而 遂晴，故作此詞。」
莫聽穿林打葉聲
何妨吟嘯且徐行
竹杖芒鞋輕勝馬    誰怕
一簑煙雨任平生
料峭春寒吹酒醒    微冷
山頭斜照卻相迎
回首向來蕭瑟處    歸去
也無風雨也無晴
--宋 。蘇東坡《定風波》

en: That year, you walked with me into
A scroll painted with clouds and mist
In the blank space, together watching distant mountains and the setting sun
With the only life I have
Playing chess against you
Will you come down?
A trace of moonlight, heaven and earth an inn for travelers
A wisp of clear breeze, a fleeting traveler through time
A pot of cloudy wine, how many red sunsets

points.zh:
夫天地者，萬物之逆旅。光陰者，百代之過客。
而浮生若夢，為歡幾何？古人秉燭夜遊，良有以也。
況陽春召我以煙景，大塊假我以文章。
會桃李之芳園，序天倫之樂事。
--唐 。李白《春夜宴桃李園序》

en: The years are a thin sheet of paper
Covered in frost, dew, and dust
Sometimes, falling leaves drift into the sound of autumn
In the afternoon, a sudden downpour
The flowers scatter down one after another, and there rises
The sound of spring shattering

points.zh: 歐姬芙（Georgia O’Keeffe, 1887 ~ 1986），美國女畫家，以巨大的花卉畫作聞名，也以一身細膩且豐盛的姿態留下令人難忘的身影。生於美國威斯康辛州，12歲時决心從事繪畫。曾在芝加哥，紐約等學畫。喜歡孤絶沙漠景色，美國西南部，德州，新墨西哥州等地，都有她作畫的足跡和意象，最後則定居於 Santa Fe 近郊的荒野。歐姬芙的作品出現的意象一律是花、骨骸、風景的局部，因而形成半抽象的構圖，亦即「部份化」的手法運用，所以雖難歸屬為純粹的抽象畫家，不過簡潔的色面，筆調平滑單純，背景空曠，倒也近似抽象繪畫的意境。況且因爲與「紐約畫派」的因緣，歐姬芙的作品也成為代表美國圖像的一部份。另外，她的作品不管是風景或花卉，往往溶入暗喻著女性器官的形式。歐姬芙不喜歡被稱為「女畫家」，要人稱她為「畫家」，由於她對性別的優越感，在畫中不時禮讚女性的圖像和意識是極為可能的。美國現代主義運動，歐姬芙發揮了相當關鍵的作用，當代許多女性崇拜她、景仰她，也因她而思考自己身為女性的時代意義。從很多事蹟可以看出她何以是當代女性追隨景仰的偶像: 一種不斷自身蛻變的堅忍和強悍，透過毫不妥協而完成自我療癒和昇華。而這種美麗的生命力，於她的畫，於她的人，始終深沉安靜地存在著，正如她喜愛的遼闊沙漠。
points.en: Georgia O'Keeffe (1887–1986), American woman painter, renowned for her large-scale flower paintings, and remembered for the delicate yet abundant presence she left behind. Born in Wisconsin, USA, she resolved at age 12 to pursue painting. She studied art in Chicago, New York, and elsewhere. Drawn to solitary desert landscapes, she left her mark and imagery across the American Southwest, Texas, New Mexico, and other places, eventually settling in the wilderness near Santa Fe. The imagery appearing in O'Keeffe's works is consistently flowers, bones, and fragments of landscape, forming semi-abstract compositions — that is, a technique of "partial" representation — so that while she is difficult to classify as a purely abstract painter, her simplified planes of color, smooth and unadorned brushwork, and open, empty backgrounds are nonetheless close to the mood of abstract painting. Moreover, owing to her association with the "New York School," O'Keeffe's works have also become part of what represents American imagery. In addition, her works, whether landscapes or flowers, often incorporate forms suggestively evoking female anatomy. O'Keeffe disliked being called a "woman painter," insisting on being called simply a "painter"; given her sense of gender pride, it is quite possible that her paintings repeatedly celebrate feminine imagery and consciousness. O'Keeffe played a pivotal role in the American modernist movement, and many contemporary women admire and look up to her, prompted by her to reflect on the meaning of their own era as women. Many episodes of her life reveal why she became an idol followed and admired by contemporary women: a resilience and toughness of constant self-transformation, achieved through uncompromising self-healing and transcendence. And this beautiful vitality, in her paintings as in her person, has always existed quietly and deeply — just like the vast desert she loved.

zh: 旅程是一片風景， 可以
en: The journey is a scene, one that can
Waking in a foreign land where the wind is still and the grass is green
Dreams enter the riverbank where fishermen's songs are softly sung
Red leaves, left for the autumn wind
Setting sun, left for the reeds
To whom is the Blue Danube left?

points.zh:
《 藍色多瑙河 ,  The Blue Danube 》
奧地利作曲家：小約翰 . 史特勞斯
Danube so blue, so bright and blue
through vale and field you flow so calm,
our Vienna greets you, you silver stream
through all the lands you merry the heart
with your beautiful shores.
Far from the Black Forest
you hurry to the sea
giving your blessing to everything.
Eastward you flow,
welcoming your brothers,
A picture of peace for all time!
Old castles looking down from high,
greet you smiling from their steep
and craggy hilltops,
and the mountains' vistas
mirror in your dancing waves.
《藍色多瑙河》是奧地利作曲家小約翰、史特勞斯 ( Johann Strauss II ) 於1867年創作的一首圓舞曲。這首圓舞曲和《維也納森林的故事》，《皇帝圓舞曲》并稱為史特勞斯的三大圓舞曲。其中以藍色多瑙河最負盛名，成為維也納華爾兹的代名詞。藍色多瑙河在1867年的巴黎世界博覽會上獲得巨大成功，從此流傳全球。如今被視為奧地利的「第二國歌」。此曲是傳統維也 納新年音樂會必奏的曲目之一。
約翰、史特勞斯的《藍色多瑙河圓舞曲》是他在奧地利帝國於普奧戰爭慘敗後，
為了讓民眾擺脫這種沮喪鬱悶的情緒，所創作出的一首象徵「維也納生命活力」
的圓舞曲。聽完這熟悉動人的旋律之後，你是否感受到希望與活力在内心波動 ?
是否彷彿也看到多瑙河岸上飄搖的垂柳，田野盡處村落的炊煙，雲霧蒸騰籠罩的
遠山，河面迷濛的淺藍水色……。
